bib.title: Can Generalist Foundation Models Outcompete Special-Purpose Tuning? Case Study in Medicine

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Can Generalist Foundation Models Outcompete Special-Purpose Tuning? Case Study in Medicine" (Medprompt). Nori, Lee, Zhang, et al. (Microsoft; Horvitz). arXiv:2311.16452v1, preprint, Nov 2023.

COVERAGE: All 21 pages, 57,530 chars, read in full (text, Tables 1-2, ablation, references skimmed). Figures 1, 4, 5, 6, 7 come through only as extracted labels, not images. I did not run the figure-caption script, so the figure-derived numbers rest on text extraction. No scan or garbling problems.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Medprompt (kNN few-shot + self-generated CoT + choice-shuffle ensemble) takes GPT-4 to 90.2% on MedQA, versus 81.7% for the simple-prompt baseline.
   number: 90.2% vs 81.7% (+~9 points); 27% error-rate reduction vs best specialist models
   setup: GPT-4 (Mar 2023 era), MedQA US 4-option (1273 questions), k=5 kNN exemplars, 5-call ensemble.
   quote: "On the MedQA dataset (USMLE exam), Medprompt produces a 9 absolute point gain in accuracy, surpassing 90% for the first time on this benchmark."
   where: p.3 (Intro); Fig 1a p.2
2. Ablation of component contributions on MedQA, layered cumulatively. CoT adds the most, then random few-shot and the ensemble.
   number: zero-shot 81.7 -> random 5-shot +2.2 -> self-generated CoT +3.4 -> kNN dynamic 5-shot +0.8 -> 5x choice-shuffle ensemble +2.1 -> 90.2
   setup: MedQA, GPT-4, k=5, 5 calls. Order is subjective, chosen by technique complexity. The authors say the techniques are not statistically independent, so the numbers are approximate. Shapley values were not computed.
   quote: "The introduction of chain-of-thought steps, as described in Section 4, contributed the most to performance (+3 .4%), followed by few-shot prompting and choice shuffle ensembling (+2.2% each)."
   where: p.14 (Sec 5.2); Fig 6 p.14
   NOTE (internal inconsistency): Fig 4 (p.10) gives running accuracies 81.7, 83.9, 87.3, 88.4, 90.2. That makes kNN +1.1 and ensemble +1.8. Fig 6 labels kNN +0.8 and ensemble +2.1. The body text says "+2.2% each" for few-shot and ensemble. Do not quote a single ensemble figure without flagging this. Fig 4 numbers: "81.7 83.9 87.3 88.4 90.2MedQA Accuracy".
3. GPT-4's self-generated CoT beats expert-crafted CoT.
   number: 86.9 vs 83.8 (+3.1)
   setup: MedQA, fixed 5-shot, no ensemble; expert CoT is the Med-PaLM 2 prompt.
   quote: "GPT-4's self-generated CoT outperforms the expert-crafted one by 3.1 absolute points."
   where: p.15 (Table 2)
4. Ensemble size and shot count: going bigger gives only a marginal gain.
   number: k=20 exemplars and 11 ensemble calls give 90.6% (+0.4) on MedQA
   setup: same as above. The default of 5 and 5 is described as a cost/accuracy balance.
   quote: "by increasing to 20 few-shot exemplars and 11 ensemble items, we achieve a further +0.4% performance on MedQA, setting a new state-of-the-art performance threshold of 90.6%."
   where: p.11 (Sec 4.4); p.14
5. State of the art on all nine MultiMedQA multiple-choice sets, with one strategy for all.
   number: MedQA 90.2 (vs Med-PaLM 2 86.5), PubMedQA 82.0 (81.8), MedMCQA dev 79.1 (72.3), MMLU Clinical 95.8 (88.7), Genetics 98.0 (92.0), Anatomy 89.6 (84.4), Prof. Medicine 95.2 (95.2), College Biology 97.9 (95.8), College Medicine 89.0 (83.2). GPT-4 5-shot MedQA is 81.4.
   setup: Table 1. Med-PaLM numbers are "choose best" per dataset and fine-tuned. The 90.2 footnote says 90.6 is the k=20, 11x setting. Professional Medicine ties rather than wins.
   quote: "By contrast, every GPT-4 reported number uses a single, consistent strategy across all datasets."
   where: p.12
6. Cost: Medprompt uses far fewer calls than Med-PaLM 2.
   number: 5 calls vs up to 44
   quote: "Med-PaLM 2's Ensemble Refinement method used as many as 44 separate inferences for a single question."
   where: p.5; abstract says "an order of magnitude fewer calls"
7. No sign of overfitting to the benchmarks through prompt iteration.
   number: 20% eyes-off holdout; 90.6% eyes-on vs 91.3% eyes-off average; eyes-off better in 6/9 datasets
   quote: "GPT-4 with Medprompt achieved an average performance of 90.6% on the eyes-on data, and an average performance of 91.3% on the eyes-off data"
   where: p.13 (Fig 5); method p.6
8. Gain transfers out of domain.
   number: +7.3% average over zero-shot on the non-medical sets, vs +7.1% on MultiMedQA
   setup: six MMLU sets (electrical engineering, machine learning, philosophy, professional accounting, professional law, professional psychology) plus two NCLEX nursing sets. Fig 7 compares zero-shot, random 5-shot and Medprompt.
   quote: "Medprompt provides an average improvement of +7 .3% over baseline zero-shot prompting."
   where: p.16
9. Mechanism, no number. Choice shuffling counters position bias and adds diversity beyond temperature sampling. The final answer is the mode over shuffled-order samples. Self-generated CoT is filtered by keeping only examples whose generated answer matches the label.
   quote: "If this answer does not match the ground truth label, we discard the sample entirely, under the assumption that we cannot trust the reasoning."
   where: p.9

Method details useful for the note: kNN over text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings, cosine distance, k=5 nearest training questions. Self-consistency is run at temperature > 0. Answer choices are shuffled before each sample. Majority vote over 5 samples. The CoT prompt template is "## Question: {{question}} {{answer_choices}} ## Answer ... Therefore, the answer is [..]" (Fig 3, p.8).

LIMITS
- Results are on multiple-choice exams only. The authors say they did not test the open-text adaptations (embedding-closest answer, or Ensemble Refinement-style concatenation).
- Possible memorization or benchmark contamination. The MELD black-box test found nothing, but "blackbox testing approaches like MELD are unable to guarantee that data has not been seen before".
- Benchmark performance does not show real-world clinical efficacy.
- Better prompting may make remaining hallucinations harder to detect.
- Bias and equity were not assessed.
- The ablation depends on ordering, and the Fig 4 / Fig 6 / text numbers conflict (see claim 2).
- The self-generated CoT filter only catches wrong final answers, not wrong reasoning that reaches the right answer.
- The comparison to Med-PaLM 2 uses "choose best" numbers.
- Needs a labeled training set for kNN exemplars and CoT generation.
- Dated: single model (GPT-4, 2023), and no non-GPT-4 models tested. Gains over modern reasoning models are not shown.

BUILDS ON
- Few-shot ICL: Brown et al. 2020.
- Chain of thought: Wei et al. 2023 (arXiv 2022).
- Self-consistency: Wang et al. 2023.
- Dynamic exemplar selection: Liu et al. 2021 ("What makes good in-context examples for GPT-3").
- Med-PaLM and Med-PaLM 2: Singhal et al. 2022 and 2023 (expert CoT, Ensemble Refinement).
- Prior GPT-4 medical study (fixed 5-shot baseline): Nori et al. 2023.
- LLMs-as-prompt-writers: Yang et al. 2023 (OPRO), Fernando et al. 2023 (Promptbreeder).
- Position bias: Zheng et al. 2023, Pezeshkpour & Hruschka 2023.
- Ensemble diversity: Caruana et al. 2004.

CODE: Algorithm 1 (p.11) in prose.
Preprocessing: for each training q, embed it, generate a CoT and an answer, and store only the correct ones.
Inference:
- Embed Q.
- Take the 5 nearest by cosine distance.
- Repeat 5 times: shuffle Q's choices, generate CoT and answer with the 5-shot context.
- Output mode of the answers.

FIGURES
- Fig 4 (p.10): stacked component contributions on MedQA. Best single picture of the additive pipeline, but its numbers conflict with Fig 6.
- Fig 6 (p.14): ablation bars with +2.2, +3.4, +0.8, +2.1.
- Fig 2 (p.8): expert CoT next to GPT-4 CoT for the same question.
- Fig 1a (p.2): MedQA timeline across models.
- Fig 7 (p.16): out-of-domain results.
- Fig 5 (p.13): eyes-on vs eyes-off split.

PROBLEMS: None embedded; no instructions found in the PDF. Figures are extracted as labels only. Fig 1a labels are garbled, and "GPT-4 base (86.1)" is unclear in context, so do not cite it. Table 1 gives GPT-4 5-shot MedQA as 81.4, while the Fig 1 simple prompt gives 81.7. These are different baselines, so do not mix them.
